title: Integration strengthens Phillips 66’s West Coast advantage
summary: Leaders discuss how the company meets the West Coast region's unique product and logistics demands.
body_markdown:
Leaders discuss how the company meets the region’s unique product and logistics demands.


The “Today and Tomorrow” series continues with a look at how Phillips 66’s integrated assets and business units work together to create value across the West Coast.


The episode offers a closer look at the people, assets and collaboration behind the products and brands customers rely on every day.


***Featuring:** Michael Andrew, VP, midstream, commercial and business development; John Field, head of brand marketing; Kim Head, SVP, global commercial operations; and Suresh Vaidyanathan, VP, aviation and renewable fuels.*


HIGHLIGHTS


**Connect**


Teams connect marine, rail and truck transportation with pipelines, terminals, refining, renewable fuels and branded outlets.


[View clip](https://player.vimeo.com/video/1227499005?h=c0858fad87&badge=0&autopause=0&player_id=0&app_id=58479)


**Deliver**


An integrated system creates flexibility to reach new customers, deliver reliable supply and strengthen supply diversity, reinforcing Phillips 66’s long-term commitment to the region and the 76 brand.


[View clip](https://player.vimeo.com/video/1227499332?h=8a71027999&badge=0&autopause=0&player_id=0&app_id=58479)


**Power**


Why integration is essential to making the West Coast system more resilient, efficient and responsive to changing market needs.


[View clip](https://player.vimeo.com/video/1227499646?h=80b6329cd7&badge=0&autopause=0&player_id=0&app_id=58479)
